clue.text: Announced shopkeeper's earner, (also not so nice or little!)

definitions.text: earner, (also not so nice or little!)
definitions.note: a grosser is something that grosses money; grosser is also the comparative of gross, nastier or fatter, the opposite of little

indicators.note: announced means spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the shopkeeper

parts.note: a grocer is a shopkeeper selling food; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A playful aside about how much a shopkeeper makes, with a bracketed joke tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter piles on definitions: a grosser earns (a film is a big grosser), and grosser also means less nice and less little, that is fatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or product that takes a lot of money is called a big grosser; as an adjective the word means nastier or heavier.

clue.text: Gossip is good when appropriate

parts.note: something that is a gas is great fun
to bag is to take or appropriate

explanation.surface: A claim that gossip is fine when the time is right.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is a person who talks too much, a chatterer or gossip.

clue.text: EU minister opening function turned up late

indicators.note: in a down answer turned up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the European Union

indicators.note: the minister is opening the function, so goes inside it

parts.note: a do is a party or function
Rev, short for Reverend, is a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A European minister arrived late to open a function.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means not arrived by the expected time, so behind schedule.

clue.text: Helping person out of Asian tram

indicators.note: out of signals the letters are made out of the given ones, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone helps a passenger out of an Asian tram.
explanation.definitionFit: A Good Samaritan, from the parable, is anyone who stops to aid a stranger in need.

clue.text: Almost the whole nation cast out again

indicators.note: almost means not quite whole, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a republic is a whole nation state
to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: Nearly a whole country expelled people once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that is out has been published, so one out again has been issued a second time.

clue.text: Nothing in set of clothes is wasted

indicators.note: in tells us the nothing goes inside the set of clothes

parts.note: an outfit is a set of clothes worn together
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A remark that an outfit with nothing in it is a waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of it is slang for drunk or stoned, and wasted is slang for the same intoxicated state.

clue.text: Private's pained expression, close to exhaustion

definitions.note: private is: personal, belonging to oneself

parts.note: ow is a cry of pain

indicators.note: close here means end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A soldier groans at being near exhaustion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier, but it is the adjective; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Your own things are personal, kept for yourself, just as private things are.

clue.text: What bit possibly can be over by Thursday?

parts.note: over as a prefix, as in over-heavy, means too

explanation.surface: A question about which piece might be finished by Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' reads as a noun, a piece, but it is the past tense of bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth are what an animal or person uses to bite, so a tooth is what bit.

clue.text: Exhausted state of female on drinking spree?

parts.note: to be on the razzle is to be out on a drinking spree

explanation.surface: A woman out on a bender ends up worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: On the razzle is British slang for out partying and drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worn to a frazzle means completely exhausted, a frazzle being that state.

clue.text: Dynamic economy initially is right to reform

indicators.note: reform means form again, so the letters are rearranged
initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Reforming a dynamic economy is said to be the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dynamic economy' suggests a tiger economy, a false trail; only 'Dynamic' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigerish means fierce and energetic like a tiger, so full of forceful drive.

clue.text: What to do with envelopes, each carried by different postmen?

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it, so the abbreviation for each goes inside
different signals the letters of postmen made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about how various postmen handle envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' looks like postmen carrying envelopes, but it is the containment signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding a sealed envelope over a kettle loosens the glue so it can be opened secretly, a classic snooping technique.

clue.text: Coin that was rectangular? Normal shape for coin!

parts.note: coins are normally round, and a round shape is the letter O
in printing and computing slang an exclamation mark is called a bang

explanation.surface: A puzzled musing on an old coin that was not round.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark is not mere punctuation: it is part of the wordplay, read as its slang name.
explanation.definitionFit: The obang was a large old Japanese gold coin of oblong shape, unlike usual round money.

clue.text: Summer featured days on the turn, shorter

indicators.note: turning round means the letters are read backwards
shorter tells us to take a shortened part of the words, a run hidden inside them

parts.note: the letters run across these two words

explanation.surface: A sad note that summer has featured days that turn shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' looks like the season, but it means one who sums.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer, read as sum-er, is someone who adds numbers up, which is just what an adder does.

clue.text: A lot of wine with curry — by chance, neither finished

indicators.note: neither word gets its last letter, so each loses its end

parts.note: a balti is a style of curry
hazard means chance, as in a game of hazard

explanation.surface: Someone describes eating curry while drinking plenty of wine, both a matter of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither finished' cuts the last letter off both BALTI and HAZARD; 'by' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A balthazar is a very large wine bottle holding sixteen standard bottles.

clue.text: Yummy sauce something recommended less for kids these days

parts.note: sauce and lip both mean cheek, impudence

parts.words: something recommended less for kids these days
parts.note: smacking children as punishment is now widely discouraged

explanation.surface: A tasty sauce, plus a comment on parenting methods out of favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-smacking describes food so delicious it makes you smack your lips, very tasty.

clue.text: Writers were emotional, upset by US jails

parts.note: felt means experienced feelings
tipped means knocked over
pen is American slang for a penitentiary, a prison

explanation.surface: Writers became emotional after American prisons rattled them.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt-tipped pens are writing implements, so they are writers in the sense of things that write.

clue.text: Working out what dockers might have done

definitions.meaning: first meaning: reasoning a conclusion out
second meaning: someone who docks pay makes a ... from it

explanation.walkthrough: 'dockers' suggests dock workers, but here they are people who dock money from wages.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both reasoned inference and an amount subtracted, as from pay.

clue.text: Yankees involved with sports plot with agents

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the radio alphabet; two of them for the plural

explanation.surface: American teams mixed up with sport in a story about spies.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy story is a thriller whose plot features secret agents.

clue.text: Game had by for example snowboarders

definitions.text: Game had by for example snowboarders

parts.words: Game had by for example snowboarders
parts.note: the word snowboarders has a boar, a pig, sitting in its middle, which describes the name of a children's game

explanation.surface: A suggestion that snowboarders have some game they play.
explanation.walkthrough: Look inside the word snowboarders: snow-BOAR-ders puts a boar in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig in the middle is a children's ball game where one player in the centre tries to intercept throws.

clue.text: Vivid reaction from drunk after endless Merlot?

indicators.note: after places the hiccup behind the shortened word
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Merlot is a variety of grape
hic is the hiccup sound of a drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk's vivid response after too much Merlot.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphic means vividly detailed, as in a graphic description.

clue.text: Sugar drop about to take effect

indicators.note: about means around, so one goes round the other

parts.note: to drop is to lose
to act is to take effect, as a drug acts

explanation.surface: A dose of sugar about to start working.
explanation.definitionFit: Lactose is the natural sugar found in milk.

clue.text: Flamboyant if unattractive topless hosts it's understood

indicators.note: hosts means holds inside, as a host does a guest
topless in a down clue means the first letter goes

parts.note: ugly means unattractive

indicators.note: understood means as heard, taking the sound of the word

parts.note: it's is pronounced with a z sound

explanation.surface: Flashy if plain-looking people host something tacitly agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitzy means showy and glamorous, so flashily extravagant.

clue.text: Source thus claiming government department's in fits

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring, a source of water

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so one word contains the other

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
MOD is the Ministry of Defence, a UK government department

explanation.surface: A source says a government department is in turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodic means occurring irregularly in bursts, just like something happening in fits and starts.

clue.text: Film about day centre

indicators.note: about means round, so the film goes round the day

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, like a mist

explanation.surface: A movie about a day centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie, but it means a thin layer, such as mist.
explanation.definitionFit: The midst is the middle or heart of something.

clue.text: Chap roughly repelled bloodsuckers

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about or roughly

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lice are parasites that feed on blood

explanation.surface: A man roughly fought off blood-sucking pests.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil is a man's name, and a chap is any man, so a name can stand for him.

clue.text: Sounded thrilled: and so to the end, off and on

indicators.note: off and on means skipping one letter and taking the next, alternately

explanation.surface: A description of thrilled sounds lasting intermittently to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To ooh is to make an exclamation of delight or wonder, as an excited audience does.

clue.text: One prompts backward solicitor: speak!

indicators.note: backward means the word for prompts is read from the end

parts.note: tips are hints or prompts
one is the Roman numeral I
a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor

explanation.surface: A person nudges a reticent lawyer to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is one who solicits trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit it out is an idiom urging someone hesitating to say what they mean at once.

clue.text: Function that could be deadly?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the abbreviation of sine, a trigonometric function
second meaning: one of the seven deadly ...

explanation.walkthrough: Sin is the written short form of sine in mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the mathematical sine abbreviation and a moral wrong, seven of which are deadly.

clue.text: Peninsula that might be Burmese poking into a bit of China

indicators.note: poking into means going inside the other piece

parts.note: the yuan is the currency unit of China
a Burmese is a breed of cat

explanation.surface: A peninsula pictured as a Burmese region pushing into China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burmese' and 'China' suggest Asian geography, but the peninsula is in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yucatan is the large peninsula of south-east Mexico separating the Gulf from the Caribbean.

clue.text: Drink, uninteresting, altered internally with spice

parts.note: gin is a spirit

indicators.note: the inside of the word is changed, its middle letters swapped

parts.note: grey means dull and uninteresting

explanation.surface: A dull drink is improved by adding spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingery means flavoured with ginger, a hot spice.
